attempts.why_died: candidate dead (BSW 2001); left open for anyone who formalizes a width lower bound to refute it

formal_statement: ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))), (∀ C ∈ F, C.card ≤ 3) → ¬ PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfiable (↑F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) → ∃ π : List (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)), PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsRefutation (↑F : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))) π ∧ ∀ C ∈ π, C.card ≤ k
plain_statement: There is a fixed k such that every unsatisfiable 3-CNF formula has a resolution refutation using only clauses of at most k literals. This is the correctness claim of the n^O(k) algorithm that saturates all resolvents of width at most k. Expected false: Ben-Sasson and Wigderson (J. ACM 48(2), 2001) give linear width lower bounds for random 3-CNF and Tseitin formulas on expanders. A refutation of this lemma kills the candidate formally.
title: Candidate 1: width-k resolution saturation decides 3-SAT
